title: Around town
goal: Name the main places in town, say where you go with au, à la, à l' and aux, and ask if there's a place nearby.

items.fr: à + le = au, à + les = aux
items.en: contractions of à with le and les (au parc, aux toilettes)

drills.explain: [[à + la]] does not change: [[à la banque]].
Before a vowel or silent h: [[à l']].

drills.prompt: “My parents live in the United States.” Which is correct?
options: Mes parents habitent à les États-Unis.
drills.explain: [[à + les]] → [[aux]]; the x links with a z sound: aux‿États-Unis.

items.fr: Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ?
items.en: Is there a pharmacy near here?
accept: Est-ce qu'il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ?
Y a-t-il une pharmacie près d'ici ?
Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici

items.note: In Québec, [[l'épicerie]] is any grocery store, even a big one, and [[faire l'épicerie]] means to do the grocery shopping. In France, [[une épicerie]] is usually a small shop.
Only for trains. A metro station is [[une station de métro]].

blocks.title: Meeting a neighbour in Montréal
blocks.context: Raj has just moved to Rosemont, a neighbourhood in Montréal. He meets Lucie outside the building.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Bonjour, madame. Je m'appelle Raj. Je suis nouveau dans le quartier.
lines.en: Hello, ma'am. My name is Raj. I'm new in the neighbourhood.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Enchanté. Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ?
lines.en: Nice to meet you. Is there a pharmacy near here?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Oui, il y a une pharmacie à côté de la banque, en face du parc.
lines.en: Yes, there's a pharmacy next to the bank, opposite the park.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Il y a un dépanneur juste là, à droite. Le supermarché est loin d'ici, mais il y a un arrêt d'autobus devant l'école.
lines.en: There's a corner store right there, on the right. The supermarket is far from here, but there's a bus stop in front of the school.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Elle est près de la gare. Moi, je vais à la bibliothèque le samedi.
lines.en: It's near the train station. I go to the library on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Et moi, je vais au supermarché le samedi ! Merci beaucoup, Lucie.
lines.en: And I go to the supermarket on Saturdays! Thank you very much, Lucie.

blocks.body: New words to understand: [[le quartier]] (the neighbourhood), [[Bienvenue !]] (Welcome!), [[juste là]] (right there), [[un dépanneur]] (a corner store in Québec; see the deep dive).

blocks.title: Going to, being at: à
blocks.body:
You met [[aller au]] and [[aller à la]] in Unit 5. [[À]] means both **to** and **at**:

- [[Je vais à la banque.]] = I'm going **to** the bank.
- [[Je suis à la banque.]] = I'm **at** the bank.
- [[Je travaille à l'hôpital.]] = I work **at** the hospital.

Just like [[de]] in the last lesson, [[à]] combines with [[le]] and [[les]].

blocks.title: À + the article
head: à + …
becomes
example
blocks.note: Compare: [[à côté du parc]] (de + le = du) and [[je vais au parc]] (à + le = au). [[À le]] and [[à les]] never appear in French.

blocks.title: Is there… near here?
blocks.pattern: Il y a + un / une + lieu + près d'ici ?
blocks.note: [[Près d'ici]] = near here; [[loin d'ici]] = far from here. [[De]] becomes [[d']] before [[ici]].

examples.fr: Il y a une boulangerie près d'ici ?
examples.en: Is there a bakery near here?

examples.fr: Oui, il y a une boulangerie en face de la poste.
examples.en: Yes, there's a bakery opposite the post office.

examples.fr: Non, il n'y a pas de banque près d'ici.
examples.en: No, there's no bank near here.
The hospital is far from here.

blocks.body:
- **Library ≠ librairie:** [[la bibliothèque]] is a library (free books to borrow). [[La librairie]] is a **bookstore**. A classic false friend!
- **Gare vs station:** [[la gare]] is for trains. For the metro, say [[la station de métro]].
- **À le:** always [[au]]: [[au supermarché]], [[au parc]].
- **Silent h:** [[l'hôpital]], [[à l'hôpital]], never [[le hôpital]].

blocks.title: Québec neighbourhood words
blocks.body:
- [[le dépanneur]]: the corner store. It sells milk, bread, snacks, and in Québec also beer and wine. Many are open late.
- [[l'autobus]]: in Québec, people often say [[l'autobus]] rather than [[le bus]], so [[l'arrêt d'autobus]] is the bus stop.
- [[la caisse]] (or [[la caisse populaire]]): many Quebecers bank at a cooperative “caisse” rather than a [[banque]].
- [[le bureau de poste]]: in Canada, many post office counters are inside a pharmacy or a store.
- [[faire l'épicerie]]: to do the groceries. In France you'd say [[faire les courses]].

examples.en: I'm going to the corner store.
On Saturdays, I do the groceries.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.tip: [[bou]] with ou, then [[lan]] is nasal; the e is silent: “boo-lahnzh-ree”.

lines.en: My parents live in the United States.
lines.tip: Liaison: aux‿États‿Unis sounds like “oh-zay-ta-zoo-nee” (with the French u).

Est-ce qu'il y a une boulangerie près d'ici ?
Y a-t-il une boulangerie près d'ici ?
blocks.explain: [[Il y a]] + [[une boulangerie]] + [[près d'ici]], with a rising voice.

blocks.prompt: The bank is opposite the park.
accept: La banque est en face du parc.
blocks.explain: [[en face de + le parc]] → [[en face du parc]].

blocks.en: The bus stop is opposite the supermarket.
blocks.explain: [[en face de]] + [[le]] → [[du]]. Careful: it's [[de]] here, not [[à]].

blocks.fr: La pharmacie est à côté de la banque.
accept: La pharmacie est à côté de la banque
blocks.explain: [[côté]] has an ô and an é.

blocks.prompt: A new neighbour asks you about the area. Tell them about three places near your home and where they are. Then say where you go on Saturdays.
checklist: Three places with il y a
Where they are (à côté de, en face de, près de…)
Je vais au / à la / à l' / aux…
A time word (le samedi, le matin…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Près d'ici, il y a une boulangerie, une pharmacie et un parc. La boulangerie est en face de la banque. La pharmacie est à côté du supermarché. Le samedi, je vais au parc avec ma fille, et le soir, je vais à la bibliothèque.
models.en: Near here there's a bakery, a pharmacy and a park. The bakery is opposite the bank. The pharmacy is next to the supermarket. On Saturdays I go to the park with my daughter, and in the evening I go to the library.

blocks.prompt: Write a short message to a friend who is moving to your city. Tell them what there is near your home and where you often go.
checklist: One place that isn't near (loin de / il n'y a pas de)
Use au, à la, à l' or aux at least twice

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Olivier ! Mon quartier est super. Il y a une épicerie, une boulangerie et un parc près de mon appartement. L'arrêt d'autobus est devant l'école. L'hôpital est loin d'ici. Le matin, je vais à la boulangerie, et le samedi, je vais au parc. À bientôt ! Amira
models.en: Hi Olivier! My neighbourhood is great. There's a grocery store, a bakery and a park near my apartment. The bus stop is in front of the school. The hospital is far from here. In the morning I go to the bakery, and on Saturdays I go to the park. See you soon! Amira

summary:
- Name twelve common places in town, with their gender
- Say where you go or are with [[au, à la, à l', aux]]
- Ask [[Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ?]] and understand the answer
- Recognize Québec words like [[le dépanneur]] and [[l'autobus]]
